propositions: Parallel compaction mutations to worktree (SNAPSHOT writes, retires, deletions) before git commit cause crashes that leave dirty tree unrecoverable by sync merge, stranding local commits and breaking attestation checks.
Tracked runtime markers (*/.archived, */.write.lock) committed before gitignore patterns were added remain as tracked dirt in every marker churn, violating the clean-tree requirement.
Sync reconverge fails on two abort variants: untracked files origin wants to create and tracked-file deletions/modifications; only the first is currently recovered.
A compaction fold interrupted mid-execution leaves worktree mutations unrolled, requiring either automated crash recovery or manual operator repair to restore clean state.
Store-wide scans (fsck, compact-all) walk archived tickets by default, causing scan cost to grow linearly with store size rather than active ticket count.
